title: Revisiting Thinning Methods for Kernel Learning Problems
abstract: arXiv:2609.07432v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Kernel methods are widely used because of their strong theoretical guarantees and empirical performance. However, their high computational cost limits their applicability to large-scale datasets. To address this shortcoming, several approaches use Maximum Mean Discrepancy to construct representative subsets that preserve the properties of the full dataset in a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space. We introduce Backward Kernel Herding, an algorithm that addresses this problem by iteratively removing points from the dataset, achieving results comparable to current state-of-the-art approaches while accelerating the subsampling process in realistic scenarios where the reduced size is less than half of the dataset. Moreover, we overcome a limitation of Kernel Thinning by proposing an extension that enables the construction of subsets of arbitrary size rather that restricting to successive halvings. translated_title: 重新审视核学习问题中的稀疏化方法
translated_abstract: 核方法因其强大的理论保证和优异的实证性能而被广泛应用。然而，其高昂的计算成本限制了其在大规模数据集上的适用性。为解决这一缺陷，若干方法使用最大均值差异来构建代表性子集，以便在再生核希尔伯特空间中保留完整数据集的性质。我们提出了反向核聚合，这是一种通过从数据集中迭代移除数据点来解决该问题的算法，在缩减规模小于数据集一半的现实场景中，能够加速子采样过程，同时取得与当前最先进方法相当的结果。此外，我们提出了一种扩展方法，克服了核稀疏化的一个限制，使算法能够构建任意大小的子集，而不再局限于逐次减半的方式。最后，我们进行了大量的实验……
tldr: 提出反向核聚合算法，通过迭代移除数据点构建代表子集，在加速子采样的同时达到与最先进方法相当的效果，并扩展核稀疏化方法使其能够构建任意大小的子集。
en_tdlr: We propose Backward Kernel Herding, which builds representative subsets by iteratively removing data points, achieving state-of-the-art comparable results while accelerating subsampling, and extend Kernel Thinning to enable construction of subsets of arbitrary size.
